ravi: Pasting a concise digest of the Orchid-11B bring-up. We ran fp16 / int7 / int5 on our QA + multi-turn CS slices. Goal: recommend routing + price-quality gates for GTN. Artifacts: https://redwood.internal/bench/orchid11b/1845554321 :link:

qa-bot: AUTO: Bulk eval complete (job id: ob-1845). Reports: QA F1 / Prec / Recall, long-answer ROUGE, hallucination rate, and per-slice GTN.

anna: High-level summary pls? where does int5 sit?

ravi: Short summary: int5 is ~45% cheaper than fp16 on unit-econ but shows measurable degradation on long, open-ended QA (hallucination +4.8pp, ROUGE-L -4.2). int7 is a middle ground (~25% cheaper) with minimal quality delta on both short QA and multi-turn CS. Latency: median/99p is surprisingly similar for int7 vs fp16; int5 shows 99p inflation on >800 token outputs.

kevin: Can you paste the unit-econ and per-call math? Product wants $/call for our canonical API usage (prompt 32 tokens, response 96 tokens).

ravi: Sure, pulled from bench cost model (includes amortized GPU + infra + net):
```
mode | $/1M tokens | $/canonical_call (32 in / 96 out) | median latency | 99p latency
fp16 | $38.2       | $0.00461                           | 110ms          | 400ms
int7 | $28.7       | $0.00346                           | 125ms          | 420ms
int5 | $20.9       | $0.00252                           | 150ms          | 720ms
```
Note: canonical_call cost = ($/1M tokens) * (128 tokens) / 1e6.

anna: For GTN, what's acceptable delta for target metrics? We can't accept more hallucinations in CS flows.

ravi: My recommendation: set different gates per route: 
- Consumer chat/short QA (<=256 tokens): default to int5. 
- Knowledge / critical CS flows and long-answer QA (>256 tokens or requires citation): route to int7; require hallucination delta <= 1.0pp and ROUGE-L delta <= 1.5. 
- If any slice is flagged as "safety/critical" route to fp16 only.

ops-bot: NOTE: observed that int5 batch kernel uses a different memory path; autoscaler steady-state may need +1 extra replica for sustained throughput.

kevin: What about hybrid routing + fallback? We should define canary flow and auto-escalation thresholds.

ravi: Canary plan: 
- Phase 1: 15% traffic to int5 on short routes (<=256). Run 48h with continuous checks. 
- Signals: GTN accuracy, hallucination delta, error rate, 95/99 latency, and KV hit % for multi-turn. 
- Escalation: If hallucination delta > 1.2pp OR error rate increase > 0.5% OR 99p latency regression > 150ms vs control -> rollback to int7 for that route. 
- Promotion: If after 48h all signals within thresholds, increase to 50% then 100% over a week.

anna: Any config toggles we should enable? KV/batching/gradual prefetch?

ravi: Ops recs: 
- Enable KV caching for sessions with >1 turn (`kv_cache_min_turns = 1`) and set `kv_eviction_policy = lru` for int5 packs. We saw ~18% 99p latency reduction on int5 when KV hit >70%.
- Use conservative batching: `max_batch_tokens = 16384` for int5 to avoid tail amplification.
- Autoscaler: min_replicas = 2, scale_up_cpu_threshold = 0.65 for int5 Dedicated pool.

kevin: Can QA/metrics own the eval harness? I'll wire product-level dashboards. Also need a quick A/B definition for GTN.

anna: I will own the GTN gating thresholds in the scorecard and update the product readiness flag to "canary". Ravi will own bench artifacts and final rec. Kevin -> dashboards/AB. Ops -> infra rollout.

qa-bot: QUEUED: Canary job ob-canary-1845 created by kevin. Expected 12h run to collect stability and hallucination signals.

kevin: Adding a small note: for billing/product optics we should publish both $/1M tokens and $/avg call to make it easy for GTN to reason about pricing. I'll add a helper in dashboard.

ravi: TL;DR: int5 yields attractive economics for short chat and read-only QA with KV-on, but int7 is safer default for mixed/long-answer flows. Start small canary for int5 on short routes with strict hallucination gating. We'll reconvene after ob-canary-1845 posts results. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
